name: Learn to knit
blurb: Four things — cast on, knit, purl, cast off — and you can make a scarf, a dishcloth and eventually anything. Knitting is repetitive in the way that makes it restful rather than dull.
gear: Smooth 5 mm needles — bamboo grips better than metal for beginners
Light-coloured aran or worsted yarn, so you can see the stitches
A darning needle for weaving in ends
steps: Learn the long-tail cast on, leaving a tail about three times the width of your project.
Learn the knit stitch and make a garter-stitch swatch until your tension stops wandering.
Learn the purl stitch, then combine them: alternate rows for stocking stitch, alternate within rows for rib.
Learn to cast off loosely — a tight cast-off is what makes hats that do not fit.
Learn to fix the two standard disasters: picking up a dropped stitch with a crochet hook, and recognising an accidental increase from knitting into the gap.
Weave in the ends properly and block the finished piece.
tips: Gaining stitches every row usually means you are knitting the yarn-over at the start. Count your stitches each row.
Death-grip tension is the beginner signature. Loosen up and the fabric evens out.
Light, smooth yarn shows its stitches. Learning on black fluffy novelty yarn is needlessly hard.
proof: A finished scarf or dishcloth with even tension, straight edges and no accidental increases.
